newsitem.title: UK: World's rich are getting richer, says report.
newsitem.headline: World's rich are getting richer, says report.

text.p: The wealth of the world's high net worth individuals (HNWIs) is forecast to exceed $24 trillion by the year 2000, said a report published today by Gemini Consulting in association with Merrill Lynch.

Gemini's World Wealth Report 1997 showed the wealth of HNWIs around the world amounted to more than $16 trillion in 1996. Over the last ten years HNWI wealth has grown at an average annual compound growth rate of eight percent.
Last year, the assets of HNWIs in Latin America achieved the highest growth rate of 22 percent as local capital markets have developed amid trade liberalisation and overall economic growth.

Asian HNWIs continued their ten-year trend of 15 percent growth and are forecast to outstrip North America as the second largest market for private banking services in the world after Europe by the year 2000, said the report.
The report also highlighted the resultant changes in the market for private banking services as clients become more sophisticated and demanding.

"Private banks must be able to cater for a client base which is increasingly mobile and diverse in its preferences for investment services," said Steven Beck, managing director of Gemini Consulting UK.
HNWIs are individuals with a net worth of at least $1 million and liquid investable assets of $0.5 million.
